verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 35.118
verses.english: Linked Discourses 35.118

verses.pali: 12. Lokakāmaguṇavagga
verses.english: 12. The World and the Kinds of Sensual Stimulation

verses.pali: Sakkapañhasutta
verses.english: The Question of Sakka

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

verses.pali: Atha kho sakko devānamindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: And then Sakka, lord of gods, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti?
verses.english: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?

verses.pali: Ko pana, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
verses.english: What is the cause, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

verses.pali: “Santi kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: “Lord of gods, there are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Saupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati …pe….
verses.english: A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

verses.pali: Santi kho, devānaminda, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
verses.english: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

verses.pali: santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: If a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging to them,

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: their consciousness has that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Saupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu no parinibbāyati.
verses.english: A mendicant with fuel for grasping does not become extinguished.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme no parinibbāyanti.
verses.english: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.

verses.pali: Santi ca kho, devānaminda, cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: There are sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti, na tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Anupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu parinibbāyati …pe….
verses.english: A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

verses.pali: Santi kho, devānaminda, jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
verses.english: There are sounds … smells … tastes … touches …

verses.pali: santi kho, devānaminda, manoviññeyyā dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā.
verses.english: ideas known by the mind, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: Tañce bhikkhu nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: If a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, and keep clinging to them,

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato na tannissitaṁ viññāṇaṁ hoti na tadupādānaṁ.
verses.english: their consciousness doesn’t have that as support and fuel for grasping.

verses.pali: Anupādāno, devānaminda, bhikkhu parinibbāyati.
verses.english: A mendicant free of grasping becomes extinguished.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, devānaminda, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
verses.english: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”

verses.pali: Pañcamaṁ.
